finding: Test 15 asserts "An unreadable corpus withholds the object by both routes, on `--status` and on `--record` alike", then names two routes: (a) an empty stored `roles_hash` on the latest round → condition 1 fails; (b) "a non-empty stored hash and the corpus unreadable now" → condition 5's equality fails. Route (b) is unbuildable on `--record`. §2.4 fixes that on `--record` condition 5 "reads that stamped value back off the just-recorded round rather than hashing the corpus a second time", so the stored hash and the "now" hash are one computation in one invocation: if the corpus is unreadable at record time the stamped hash is empty (route a), and there is no invocation in which a `--record` round carries a non-empty stored hash while the same invocation's corpus read fails. The "on `--record` alike" clause therefore cannot be satisfied for route (b), and an implementer will either drop the assertion or wire condition 5 on `--record` to a second, freshly computed hash — which §2.4 explicitly forbids.

finding: §2.2 requires role_streaks to be 'an emitted empty array, never null and never an omitted key', but test 17 — the only test of the empty case — asserts only that 'role_streaks is []'. Every other shape this release adds has the discrimination pinned in its own test: test 20 ('open_roles is [] — neither absent nor null'), test 22 ('an implementation emitting "divergence": null fails'), test 41 ('The null half is the discriminating one'). A decoded-slice assertion of length zero passes on null, so two engineers write assertions that disagree on exactly the nil-slice defect this repository records as recurring. spec_coverage_clean_rounds has the same gap: its 'explicit JSON null, never an omitted key' rule is asserted only through test 29's --compact fixture ('keeps the key'), never on a plain --status/--record fixture.

resolved.evidence: Addressed in the round-12 spec revision, the final review round of this cycle by the operator's decision. The single high finding and four of the mediums were one leftover: round 11 rewrote condition 5 to plain equality and deleted its non-emptiness terms, but the paragraph describing how each output sources the hash still explained those terms and named them load-bearing. That paragraph now says what is true -- the equality holds by construction on --record, so condition 5 constrains --status alone exactly as condition 3 does, and an unreadable corpus at record time is caught by SS2.1's fourth cause through condition 1 instead. Test 15 is split accordingly: route 1 on both outputs, route 2 on --status only, since --record stamps and reads one hash in one invocation and cannot reach it. SS2.1 fixes precedence within the hash test (empty before differing) and explains why the table has five rows for four causes; the second wording's justification is corrected -- it exists because naming an empty hash a different corpus would assert a corpus change that may never have happened. SS3.1 names the blank-cmd rejection cause a fixture needs and records that next_action's over-specification comment describes the unregistered case. SS2.1's walked-segment definition no longer forward-references its own consumer. Test 17 asserts role_streaks against raw JSON so a nil slice serializing as null fails, and SS6.1's duplicated opening sentence is removed. Not fixed and carried into implementation: nothing blocking; the surviving items are prose-level and the code is the better place to settle them.

suggestion: Give test 17 the wording tests 20/41 use — role_streaks is an emitted empty array, not null and not an absent key, asserted over the raw JSON — and add the same key-present-with-null assertion for spec_coverage_clean_rounds on a non-compact fixture.

finding: §6.1's opening paragraph states the same sentence twice, verbatim: it opens with "No entry is invalidated — that is the finding, not an omission: this release adds fields and filters rather than changing a shape an existing test asserts, so every entry below states what stays valid and where the new coverage sits beside it." and then closes the same paragraph with that identical sentence after the two-searches sentence. It is a copy-paste artifact, not emphasis: the two copies carry no differing word. tp's own `duplicate-paragraph` lint cannot catch it, because both copies sit inside one blank-line-separated paragraph rather than in two consecutive ones, so nothing mechanical will remove it. The cost is not cosmetic under this lens: §6.1 is section text that a decomposer reads and that `source_sections`-derived `spec_excerpt` will replay into every task anchored there, so the duplicated ~45 words are paid again on each of those payloads, and a reader who cannot tell a deliberate restatement from an editing accident has to re-read the paragraph to confirm the two copies really are identical.

finding: §2.1 announces "Five definitions govern everything in §2" and renders them as one bullet list, but the list is broken after the fourth bullet by a full non-bulleted paragraph ("Treating empty as incomparable rather than as a string to compare is the whole point ..."), after which the fifth bullet ("The walked segment") resumes. Read as markdown this is two lists with a paragraph between them, so the fifth definition is severed from the enumeration it belongs to, and the intervening paragraph reads as rationale attached to the section rather than to bullet 4 whose rule it justifies. A reader (or a task decomposing §2.1's definitions one per acceptance item) counts four definitions plus an orphan.

finding: §2.1's fifth definition scopes the segment to rounds tp reads: "**The walked segment** is the trailing run of recorded rounds tp actually loads". The advisory rule is then scoped to that segment: "A round in the walked segment that contributes no rows emits one advisory". But the same section fixes that the fourth cause is "decided first, because it needs no file read" — so a round dropped for a differing or empty stored `roles_hash` is never loaded, falls outside the segment as defined, and by the letter of the advisory rule emits nothing. That contradicts the two corpus rows of the §2.1 table and §6 tests 11 and 12, which require exactly those wordings for exactly those rounds.

finding: §2.4 justifies condition 5 with "it fails when the corpus has since changed or become unreadable — the latter because an unreadable corpus hashes to an empty string". §2.1 states the same fact in its precise form — "a role file left unreadable across several records stamps `""` on every one of them" — and only that form is true: an empty hash arises when an individual role file cannot be read, not when the corpus directory as a whole is unreadable or absent, which yields the `builtin` sentinel instead. The generalized wording, repeated as a fixture instruction in §6 test 15 ("the corpus unreadable now, the freshly computed hash is empty"), leaves the fixture underdetermined: a test that makes the *directory* unreadable gets a non-empty sentinel and the stated mechanism does not hold, even though the assertion happens to survive by inequality.
